mechanism_claims.claim_text: Serrulin has source-reviewed phenotype evidence for growth inhibition across the listed bacterial/fungal/yeast targets, but the paper does not identify a common molecular target or mode of action.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The primary text states that further experiments are needed to elucidate mechanism; do not promote MIC activity to direct mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Human erythrocyte hemolysis testing supports low hemolytic/cytotoxic effect at the tested maximum; this is toxicity/selectivity evidence, not a mechanism-of-action assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Supplementary Figure S1 is a plotted curve; exact tabular percent hemolysis values are not locally available.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Mass spectrometry and sequence comparison support serrulin as a glycine-rich AMP-like peptide with sequence similarity context and reported C-terminal modification context, but no cellular target is demonstrated.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Sequence similarity to other AMPs is context evidence only and is not treated as direct mechanism.

mechanism_summary: Source review supports antimicrobial phenotype and sequence-similarity context, while preserving the paper-level caveat that the molecular target/mode of action was not determined.
